title: Integrated structural analysis for geothermal exploration using remote sensing and aeromagnetic data
author: Rafiq, Abu-Mahfouz, et al.
materials: The initial standard deviation calculation performed within the CET analysis is particularly advantageous because it quantitatively assesses variations in magnetic data, allowing for the identification of significant structural features against background noise. Furthermore, the Lineation Detection and Amplitude Thresholding routines enable a multi-scaled analysis that can effectively differentiate between major and minor lineaments. This flexibility means that the analysis can be tailored to the specific geophysical characteristics of the study area, optimizing the detection process.

steps.title: Acquire and preprocess datasets
steps.instruction: Obtain Landsat‑8 multispectral imagery, Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) at 30 m and 12 m resolution, and airborne magnetic data in reduced‑to‑pole (RTP) format supplied by the Saudi Geological Survey. Apply radiometric corrections to the Landsat imagery, smooth the DEMs, and standardize the magnetic data before analysis.

substeps.instruction: Download Landsat‑8 scenes covering the study area.
Download DEMs (30 m and 12 m) for the same area.
Obtain RTP magnetic data from SGS.
Perform radiometric correction on the satellite images.
Smooth DEMs to reduce high‑frequency noise.
Normalize magnetic data to a common scale.

steps.title: Extract surface lineaments
steps.instruction: Run automated lineament extraction on the Landsat‑8 imagery and DEMs using the latest Catalyst version of PCI Geomatics. Apply directional filters with a 3 × 3 convolution window to obtain the shortest lineament length and set the Line Module parameters as follows: RADI = 10, DTHR = 20, FTHR = 3, GTHR = 100, ATHR = 30, LTHR = 30. Export the resulting synthetic lineament map.

substeps.instruction: Open Catalyst PCI Geomatics and load the pre‑processed imagery and DEMs.
Activate directional filters (3 × 3 window) for lineament enhancement.
Enter the Line Module settings: RADI10, DTHR20, FTHR3, GTHR100, ATHR30, LTHR30.
Run the automated extraction routine.
Save the generated lineament layer.

steps.title: Clean and augment surface lineaments
steps.instruction: Use GIS tools to remove redundant lineaments (those appearing more than once) and to eliminate features derived from hydrographic networks, human activities, or illogical patterns. Manually digitize larger lineaments that were missed by the automated process on the DEM, then produce a final cleaned lineament density map.

substeps.instruction: Identify and delete duplicate lineaments using attribute queries.
Overlay hydrographic and infrastructure layers; delete intersecting lineaments.
Manually trace large lineaments visible on the DEM but absent from the automated output.
Re‑calculate lineament density after cleaning.

steps.title: Calculate surface fracture density
steps.instruction: Compute Fault Fracture Density (FFD) for each grid cell using the equation FD = total length of lineaments (km) / cell area (km²). Generate a spatial density map with ArcGIS or equivalent software.

substeps.instruction: Divide the study area into a regular grid (choose cell size).
Sum the lengths of all lineaments within each cell (convert to km).
Divide each sum by the cell area in km² to obtain FD.
Map the FD values to visualize density zones.

steps.title: Extract subsurface lineaments
steps.instruction: Load the RTP magnetic data into Seequent Oasis Montaj with the CET Grid Analysis extension (developed by the University of Western Australia). Perform texture analysis by calculating the standard deviation σ = √[ Σ (X‑x̄)² / (n‑1) ]. Apply the Lineation Detection algorithm (Kovesi default), selecting either Phase Symmetry or Phase Congruency. The 2‑D grid is split into 1‑D profiles and analyzed over multiple directions and scales; set SymmetryPoint to the minimum or maximum value in the frequency domain as appropriate. Finally, run Amplitude Thresholding, choosing a high threshold for major regional lineaments and a low threshold for local features, and vectorize the resulting ridges to obtain a thinned straight‑line feature map.

substeps.instruction: Import RTP magnetic grid into Oasis Montaj.
Activate CET Grid Analysis and run the Texture Analysis module to compute σ.
Open the Lineation Detection tool; select Phase Symmetry (or Phase Congruency).
Configure profile direction and scale parameters; set SymmetryPoint = minimum/maximum frequency value.
Execute the detection algorithm to highlight linear features.
Run the Amplitude Thresholding routine; set a high threshold for regional lineaments, a low threshold for local lineaments.
Apply the Lineation Vectorization step to convert ridges to vector lineaments.

steps.title: Compute subsurface fracture density
steps.instruction: Using the vectorized subsurface lineaments, calculate fault density per grid cell with the formula Density = Number of lineaments in the cell / cell area (km²). Produce a subsurface FFD map.

substeps.instruction: Create the same grid used for surface analysis.
Count the vectorized lineaments intersecting each cell.
Divide the count by the cell area (km²).
Map the resulting density values.

steps.title: Integrate and compare density maps
steps.instruction: Overlay the surface and subsurface FFD maps to identify high‑density zones that may indicate increased permeability. Perform orientation analysis (e.g., rose diagrams) on both datasets to compare lineament trends and construct an integrated structural model.

substeps.instruction: Stack the surface and subsurface density rasters in GIS.
Highlight cells with the highest combined density values.
Generate rose diagrams for surface and subsurface lineament azimuths.
Interpret similarities and discrepancies to build the final structural model.

description:
1.
Data Acquisition and Preprocessing
○Begin by acquiring Landsat-8 imagery, Digital Elevation Models (DEMs), and airborne magnetic data.○Proceed with data preprocessing, which includes applying radiometric corrections, smoothing the DEMs, and standardizing the magnetic data.
2.
Lineament Extraction
○Surface Lineaments: Utilize Catalyst PCI Geomatics software to automate the extraction of surface lineaments using directional filters, complemented by manual extraction with ArcGIS software. Fine-tune the extraction parameters, remove redundant lineaments, and eliminate irrelevant features to ensure accuracy.○Subsurface Lineaments: Detect subsurface structural lineaments through CET grid analysis in Seequent Oasis Montaj. Enhance textures and apply edge detection techniques to identify both major and minor lineaments.
3.
Lineament Density Mapping
○Create Fault Fracture Density (FFD) maps for both surface and subsurface lineaments by calculating the lineament length per grid cell area using ArcGIS software.○Identify high-density zones, which indicate regions of increased permeability within the study area.
4.
Integration & Comparison
○Integrate the surface and subsurface lineament data, placing particular emphasis on the high FFD zones identified in the previous step.○Compare the trends of the lineament orientations to uncover correlations and discrepancies, culminating in the development of a comprehensive structural model (refer to Fig. 1).Fig. 1Workflow of the new protocol for surface-subsurface structural analysis of the geothermal field using integrated remotely sensed and aeromagnetic geophysical data. Note: the magnetic map and Landsat imagery used in this figure are for protocol demonstration purposes only.Fig 1 One of the primary limitations of our protocol is the automation of the lineament detection process.
